scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: A narrow prototype
scenes.caption: Aditi proposes a Decision Lab prototype for fictional strips. Its single input is a supplied contrast value, and its output suggests review or pass to a teacher. It cannot certify equipment, diagnose faults or make decisions about real people.
scenes.speech: Aditi proposes a Decision Lab prototype for fictional strips. Its single input is a supplied contrast value, and its output suggests review or pass to a teacher. It cannot certify equipment, diagnose faults or make decisions about real people.
scenes.dialogue: Write what this prototype is for.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: Train before validation
scenes.caption: Vihaan selects training examples 2→review and 8→pass. The model copies the nearest value’s label, abstaining on conflicting ties. Separate visible validation inputs 3,4,6,9 produce review,review,pass,pass. Their checked labels agree, but these are development results.
scenes.speech: Vihaan selects training examples 2→review and 8→pass. The model copies the nearest value’s label, abstaining on conflicting ties. Separate visible validation inputs 3,4,6,9 produce review,review,pass,pass. Their checked labels agree, but these are development results.
scenes.dialogue: Keep training and visible validation separate.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: The queue is real work
scenes.caption: Every review or abstention requires a human check. On the normal validation batch, the queue contains 2 strips, matching the teacher’s capacity of 2. Aditi counts outputs; correct predictions still require inspections.
scenes.speech: Every review or abstention requires a human check. On the normal validation batch, the queue contains 2 strips, matching the teacher’s capacity of 2. Aditi counts outputs; correct predictions still require inspections.
scenes.dialogue: Correct predictions can still create work.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Bound the proposed use
scenes.caption: Choose a model-card entry retaining the narrow task, actual development evidence and teacher responsibility. The allowed input range is 0 through 10. Their stop rule pauses the whole batch if an input leaves that range or required review exceeds available capacity.
scenes.speech: Choose a model-card entry retaining the narrow task, actual development evidence and teacher responsibility. The allowed input range is 0 through 10. Their stop rule pauses the whole batch if an input leaves that range or required review exceeds available capacity.
scenes.dialogue: Limits need an action and an owner.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: A changed batch arrives
scenes.caption: The changed batch contains 3,5,6,20. The model abstains at 5 and predicts pass at 20, but extrapolation is outside the stated input range. Vihaan triggers the stop rule immediately; the numerical output cannot authorise the out-of-range strip.

scenes.dialogue: A prediction cannot override the stop rule.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Hand over unresolved evidence
scenes.caption: The teacher receives the paused batch and its model card. Fresh evaluation after freezing remains unresolved, alongside monitoring and fallback. A classroom validation success is recorded accurately while the notebook leaves any real deployment decision with responsible human review.
